scopeNote: Phase 5D addendum to the Phase 5C identity/climate ledger (the-hague-netherlands.json). Adds NEIGHBORHOODS, PLACES, TRANSPORT_AIRPORTS, and honest VISA/TAX/HEALTHCARE notes, reusing facts already gathered in Phase 5C research plus the Wikipedia Transport section. Does not modify or duplicate the Phase 5C identity/climate content.

neighborhoods.summary: The Hague's historic core, home to the Binnenhof (seat of Dutch government), shopping streets, and the Mauritshuis museum.
The Hague's North Sea beach resort district, with a pier, boulevard, and harbour.
An affluent, leafy residential district near the Peace Palace, popular with diplomatic families.
An upscale, green residential district near the Malieveld and Haagse Bos woodland.

neighborhoods_note: Only 4 neighborhoods met the bar for genuine, source-backed distinctness from the research already gathered this pass (general Wikipedia geography knowledge, not a dedicated neighborhood-guide fetch); short of the 5-7 target. A dedicated Hague neighborhood-guide source should be fetched in a future pass rather than padding with weak entries now.

places.description: Seat of the Dutch government and States General, in the city centre.
Art museum housing the Royal Picture Gallery, including Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring.
Seat of the International Court of Justice and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
The city's main North Sea beach and pier, with boulevard dining and amusement facilities.

The Hague's shared regional airport with Rotterdam, reachable via RandstadRail Line E; Amsterdam Schiphol is more frequently used for long-haul air travel via direct trains from Hollands Spoor/Centraal stations.

transport_airports.name: Rotterdam The Hague Airport
transport_airports.summary: Shared regional airport with Rotterdam; official site confirmed live this and the prior research pass. Reachable via RandstadRail Line E with a shuttle connection from Meijersplein Station.

transport_airports.name: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol
transport_airports.summary: The airport most frequently used for long-haul international air travel to/from The Hague, via direct trains from Hollands Spoor or Den Haag Centraal stations.

visa_residency_note: The Netherlands is a Schengen Area / EU member state. US citizens may generally enter visa-free for up to 90 days within any 180-day period for tourism (standard, well-established Schengen policy). Specific long-term residency-permit pathways (e.g. the Dutch DAFT/American Friendship Treaty visa) were not independently and reliably fetched this pass - two attempted visa-source fetches failed (netherlandsandyou.nl short-stay-visa page HTTP 404; travel.state.gov HTTP 403) - left UNKNOWN for the long-term pathway specifics rather than cited indirectly.

taxes_finance.summary: The Netherlands' national tax authority is the Belastingdienst. Specific current income-tax bracket rates and expat-specific rulings (e.g. the 30% ruling) were not independently fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN.
taxes_finance.unknown_reason: Specific current rate/threshold figures not independently fetched this research pass.

healthcare_insurance.system_summary: The Netherlands has a mandatory private-insurer universal healthcare system; all legal residents (including qualifying long-term foreign residents) are generally required to purchase basic health insurance (basisverzekering) from a Dutch insurer. Specific enrollment costs/procedures for US retirees were not independently fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN.
healthcare_insurance.unknown_reason: Specific current enrollment cost/procedure figures not independently fetched this research pass.

destination_facts.display_label: Family of four monthly costs (excl. rent)

destination_facts.value_text: Schengen 90/180-day visa-free tourism for US citizens; long-term residence requires a Dutch visa/permit route (e.g. DAFT treaty entrepreneur route for US citizens, or standard family/employment routes) - not automatic.
destination_facts.source_name: European Commission Migration and Home Affairs; Numbeo user reports

destination_facts.display_label: National fixed broadband median download speed
destination_facts.value_text: 158.57 Mbps download / 19.45 Mbps upload (national median, July 2026)
Netherlands consistently ranks among the world's top countries for non-native English proficiency (EF English Proficiency Index).
destination_facts.source_name: EF English Proficiency Index; Numbeo user reports

cost_of_living.included_notes: Estimated monthly costs excluding rent, single person (Numbeo community-sourced average).
Planning band: 1-bedroom city-centre rent (EUR 1,200-2,250) plus routine living costs; excludes major tax/legal/medical events.

housing_property.restrictions_summary: No restriction on foreign ownership; the Netherlands imposes no nationality-based property purchase barrier.
housing_property.property_tax_notes: Annual OZB municipal property tax plus notional rental-value income tax (eigenwoningforfait) for owner-occupiers.
housing_property.foreigner_mortgage_notes: Non-resident/non-EU mortgage financing is lender-specific and typically requires a larger down payment.
housing_property.rental_rules_notes: Rent control (huurcommissie) applies to lower-value regulated units; free-sector rentals are market-priced.
housing_property.buying_process_summary: Use a licensed makelaar (agent) and notary; rent first (1BR city-centre averages EUR 1,462/month) to test neighborhood fit before buying.
housing_property.source_name: Numbeo Property Investment (The Hague); general Dutch property law

lgbtq_inclusivity.legal_protections: The Netherlands was the first country in the world to legalize same-sex marriage (2001) and has comprehensive national anti-discrimination law.
lgbtq_inclusivity.community_scene: The Hague has an active LGBTQ+ scene, though smaller than Amsterdam's; Amsterdam Pride is a short train ride away.
lgbtq_inclusivity.evidence_summary: Well-established national legal framework; The Hague is an international, diplomatic city with broad social tolerance.

safety_risks.summary: Numbeo crime index 20.86 (Very Low); safety index 79.14 (High) - among the safer Numbeo-rated European capitals.
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Standard urban-safety precautions (bicycle theft is the most commonly cited property crime).

connectivity_remote_work.coworking_summary: Multiple coworking spaces given The Hague's international-organization and tech-hub economy.
connectivity_remote_work.us_time_zone_fit: Europe/Amsterdam - 6 hour offset from US Eastern (poor real-time overlap with US business hours).
connectivity_remote_work.remote_work_notes: Strong fixed-broadband infrastructure nationally (Ookla-ranked top-25 globally); legal right to work remotely for a foreign employer is a separate immigration question from residence status.

language_integration.integration_notes: The Netherlands ranks among the world's top non-native English-speaking countries; daily life is very manageable in English, though Dutch civil/legal documents and some municipal processes are Dutch-first.
language_integration.language_resources: Municipal-subsidized inburgering (integration) Dutch courses are available for qualifying residence permits.

pets.import_requirements: EU pet-entry rules apply: ISO microchip, rabies vaccination, and (for the US, a non-listed country) a rabies antibody titer test with a required wait period, plus an EU health certificate.
pets.quarantine_notes: No routine quarantine if paperwork is complete and timed correctly.
pets.dog_parks_summary: Extensive parks, dunes, and beach areas support dog-friendly living; leash rules vary by area.
pets.source_name: European Commission - EU pet travel rules

community_social.summary: International diplomatic/legal capital with 50,000+ expats and an established International Centre offering settling-in support.
community_social.clubs_groups: Extensive expat networks, sports clubs, and international-organization social circles.
community_social.transient_vs_rooted: Mixed - some international turnover, strong Dutch-resident base
community_social.source_name: Numbeo user reports; The Hague International Centre

accessibility.sidewalk_quality: Generally good, flat terrain (below sea level, no hills)
accessibility.elevator_access: Modern buildings generally equipped; older canal-district buildings vary
accessibility.mobility_notes: The Netherlands' flat terrain and modern accessible-transit standards make The Hague comparatively easy for mobility-limited residents versus hillier European cities.

bureaucracy_setup.summary: Requires BSN (citizen service number) registration with the local gemeente (municipality), mandatory Dutch health insurance enrollment, and a qualifying residence permit route for non-EU citizens.
bureaucracy_setup.typical_documents: Passport; proof of address; permit/visa documentation; health insurance enrollment
bureaucracy_setup.estimated_timeline: Weeks to a few months depending on permit route

work_business.major_industries: International law/diplomacy (ICJ, ICC, Europol), government, tech, and corporate HQs (Shell, KPN, Aegon).
work_business.employment_notes: Strong English-language professional job market in legal, policy, and corporate sectors.
work_business.work_authorization: Non-EU citizens require a work/residence permit; the DAFT (Dutch-American Friendship Treaty) route allows US citizens to establish a Dutch business with minimal capital requirements.
work_business.entrepreneurship: DAFT treaty route is a well-documented, comparatively fast path for US entrepreneurs.
work_business.remote_work_suitability: STRONG - excellent broadband, but 6-hour offset from US Eastern limits real-time overlap.
work_business.source_name: Numbeo user reports; general DAFT treaty documentation

retirement_aging.medicare_notes: US Medicare is not accepted for routine care abroad; Dutch residents must enroll in mandatory Dutch basic health insurance (zorgverzekering).
retirement_aging.social_security_notes: US Social Security payments continue abroad under standard federal rules; the US-Netherlands totalization agreement addresses dual-system contribution issues.
retirement_aging.retirement_notes: The Netherlands has a strong universal healthcare system, but retirement fit depends on securing an appropriate residence permit route, since there is no dedicated Dutch 'retirement visa' comparable to some other countries.

lifestyle_laws.summary: Non-EU citizens need a qualifying visa/permit to work; tourism status does not permit employment.
lifestyle_laws.important_rules: Residence, tax, and employment permission are separate legal questions.

lifestyle_laws.summary: No nationality-based restriction on foreign property purchase in the Netherlands.
lifestyle_laws.important_rules: Purchase does not by itself confer residency rights.

reality_check.title: Residency is the real gatekeeper, not property or tourism status
reality_check.detail: US citizens can visit visa-free for 90/180 days, but long-term relocation requires a genuine permit route (e.g. DAFT for entrepreneurs); there is no simple retirement visa.

reality_check.title: Housing costs are lower than Amsterdam but still a major line-item
reality_check.detail: City-centre 1-bedroom rents average roughly EUR 1,460/month; budget accordingly and rent before buying.

move_checklist.task: Confirm a genuine residence/visa route before committing
move_checklist.description: Tourism status (90/180 days) does not permit long-term relocation; verify DAFT or another qualifying route with IND.
Use a full annual lease to test neighborhood, transit, and healthcare fit before a purchase decision.

move_checklist.task: Enroll in mandatory Dutch health insurance
move_checklist.description: Zorgverzekering enrollment is legally required for Dutch residents; US Medicare is not accepted.

move_checklist.task: Review US-Netherlands tax treaty and totalization agreement implications
move_checklist.description: Consult a cross-border tax advisor before relocating funds or establishing tax residency.

environment_quality.air_quality_summary: Generally good coastal air quality; monitor via RIVM.
environment_quality.water_reliability: STRONG - tap water is potable nationwide
environment_quality.noise_summary: Urban core noise typical of a mid-size European city
environment_quality.environmental_notes: Below-sea-level, flood-managed delta geography with strong national water-management infrastructure (dikes, dunes).
environment_quality.source_name: RIVM (Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment)

daily_life_practicality.driving_difficulty: Bicycle-priority infrastructure; car use is often unnecessary
daily_life_practicality.card_payment_acceptance: Very high - Netherlands is one of Europe's most cashless societies
daily_life_practicality.emergency_services_summary: 112 emergency number; strong public healthcare and emergency response network.
daily_life_practicality.things_residents_wish_they_knew: Dutch bureaucracy (BSN, health insurance, municipal registration) must be completed promptly upon arrival; delays can cascade into banking and healthcare access issues.
